Yet it was clear by then that many economies—particularly in Latin America and the Middle East—had remained stuck for decades, despite their efforts to rise to high-income status. “Middle-income trap” is now a popular phrase: it results in tens of thousands of Google search references. And it is fre- quently on the tongues of academics and politicians from developing countries—in Latin America and South Asia and just about every place in between. A decade ago, in “The Middle-Income Trap Turns Ten,” Brookings Institution econo- mist Homi Kharas and I reviewed the burgeoning literature that An East Asian Renaissance had inspired.
